item.text:
**Verdict:** Mixed, leaning negative. Jokowi did help institutionalize some durable social-service machinery, especially in health insurance and social protection, but the evidence is narrower than a full cross-society institutional legacy and is offset by persistent inequality, weak access in remote areas, and broader patronage/rights problems.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Indonesia](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) - World Health Organization, 2024. Indonesia’s health system had 90% coverage, lower out-of-pocket costs, better access regardless of gender/age/disability, and more efficient, transparent resource management. This is strong evidence that Jokowi helped sustain a rule-based institution that could outlast his personal rule. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.8`, `6B.4`, `6B.7`.

- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) - World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. Mobile JKN simplified registration, supported informal-sector contributions, and reduced BPJS administrative costs, while facing digital-divide limits. This supports durable institutional upgrading rather than one-off patronage. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.4`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`.

- [Sistem Registrasi Sosial Ekonomi Terpadu untuk Indonesia](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/id/kebijakan-sosial/laporan/sistem-registrasi-sosial-ekonomi-terpadu-untuk-indonesia) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024. Regsosek was designed to improve targeting, delivery, accountability, and transparency for social protection, using a national socioeconomic registry to reach eligible households more consistently. This is one of the clearest signs of a durable social institution being built beyond any single leader. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.7`, `6B.4`, `6B.8`.

- [Beban Lebih Ringan, Pelayanan Lebih Baik: Kemenkes dan WHO Mempercepat Redistribusi JKN](https://www.who.int/indonesia/id/news/detail/29-10-2024-less-burden--better-care--moh-and-who-accelerate-jkn-redistribution) - World Health Organization Indonesia, 2024-10-29. The JKN redistribution mechanism used workload ratios, quality standards, monitoring, and patient choice to rebalance care across facilities. That is evidence of institutional design aimed at surviving politics and improving service quality over time. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.4`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`.

- [The Care Economy in Indonesia: A Pathway for Women’s Economic Participation and Social Well-being](https://www.worldbank.org/en/events/2024/08/28/report-launch-event-the-care-economy-in-indonesia) - World Bank, 2024-08-28. The care-economy roadmap linked childcare, parental-leave reform, and women’s labor-force participation to a longer-term institutional agenda for families and children. This is positive but still mostly programmatic rather than proof of a fully durable settlement. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.8`.

- [Indonesia - Learning Poverty Brief 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099082924151529593) - World Bank/UNESCO, 2024-04-01. The brief says learning poverty remained a major threat to human capital and poverty reduction, showing that education opportunity was still not institutionalized broadly enough. This is negative evidence against a fully durable social-institution record. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.8`.

- [Social Protection Inclusion in Indonesia’s Remote Areas - Identifying and Addressing Gaps and Challenges](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099062624071020814) - World Bank, 2024-06-01. The report found poor and vulnerable households in remote areas still faced barriers to accessing social protection. That weakens the claim that social institutions had become durable and uniformly inclusive nationwide. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.4`.

- [Indonesia’s democracy icon leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14. Reuters’ end-of-term analysis says Jokowi left patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity. This is broad but important negative background for a claim that durable institutions were strengthened more than personal and family networks. QIDs: `6B.9`; also `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `4B.2`.

**Search Gap**
- I found the strongest durability evidence in health insurance, social protection, and care-economy/education-adjacent reforms.
- I did not find equally strong 2024 evidence of broad, cross-sector institution-building in housing, labor markets, or local government that clearly outlives Jokowi’s personal rule.
- The negative evidence is mostly indirect on durability: persistent inequality, weak access in remote areas, and patronage/dynastic politics rather than a single definitive collapse of institutions.
